newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: RESEARCH ALERT - First Holdings rated buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - First Holdings rated buy.

text.p: First Philippine Holdings Corp was rated a buy on Friday by Angping & Associates Securities Inc following news it will develop a 300-hectare industrial estate in joint venture with Sumitomo Corp of Japan.

"This is just one of many diversification plans of First Holdings in order to boost its earnings base and improve the revenue mix, and we see no severe downside risk in this particular segment of the property sector...," Angping Securities said in an advisory to clients.

It added the prospects for those wishing to engage in industrial estate projects seem very promising as the country gears itself as an alternative, less expensive relocation site for large multinational manufacturing firms.
For the fiscal year ending June 30, 1997, First Philippine Holdings was projected to make recurring earnings of 879 million pesos, a 36 percent improvement from the last fiscal year, Angping said.

By 1998 when the impact of the industrial estate and other infrastructure projects of First Philippine Holdings would take effect, earnings could grow by 87.8 percent to 1.65 billion pesos, the brokerage house said.

It placed forecast earnings per share of 3.94 pesos for next year and 7.40 pesos for 1998. That would put the Class B shares of the company at 14.3 and 7.6 times the two years' forecast earnings, Angping Securities said.
First Philippine Holdings B shares closed at 56 pesos on Friday, 50 centavos lower.
